It's full-time!!

The Black Ferns have recorded a 40-5 victory over the Wallaroos!

It was a deserved victory from the visitors, who scored six tries to one in wet conditions at Sunshine Coast Stadium.

They retain their Pacific Four Series crown and keep hold of the O'Reilly Cup.

That's the Black Ferns' 30th win over the Wallaroos, who are yet to post a victory over their trans-Tasman rivals.

By Luke Pentony

The Black Ferns thought they had a try after Tara Turner seemingly won the race to the ball in the in-goal area following a kick ahead.

But Ava Wereta got a hand to the ball for the Wallaroos, and the try was disallowed.

By Luke Pentony

There is no lack of effort from the Wallaroos.

They've just come up against a team in a different class to where they are at this stage.

Can they find a late try to give their fans something to cheer about?

By Luke Pentony

The Black Ferns are eyeing off the half-century on the scoreboard.

They had a entry inside the Wallaroos' half but the ball went to ground to give the home side a scrum field.

By Luke Pentony

The Wallaroos had a five-metre scrum on their feed but gave up a penalty at the set-piece following a dominant shove from the Black Ferns.

The scrum was just to the left of the posts, so the Wallaroos had an ideal position to launch an attack.

By Luke Pentony

As the rain pours down at Sunshine Coast Stadium, Wallaroos winger Desiree Miller once again showed what an attacking threat she is for the hosts.

She helped the Wallaroos earn an entry inside the Black Ferns' 22.

Key Event

By Luke Pentony

A fitting moment for Black Ferns lock Laura Bayfield as she crosses for a try.

Bayfield is a captain in the New Zealand Army, and she spoke during the week of the significance of tonight's Test.

She scored out on the right edge after the Black Ferns launched a counter-attack movement against a tiring Wallaroos defence.

With the conversion, the visitors lead 40-5.

Key Event

By Luke Pentony

Black Ferns go over again!

This time is was winger Justine McGregor, who finished off a movement to touch down in the right corner for her first Test try.

Once more, the Black Ferns showed patience by building pressure in phase play, leaving the Wallaroos' defence stretched out on the flank.

The conversion attempt from out wide was unsuccessful.

The Black Ferns lead 33-5.

By Luke Pentony

The Wallaroos and Black Ferns have been guilty of coughing up possession so far in the second half.

The Black Ferns are in a confident mood, however, as they haven't packed away their offload game.

It's a risk in terms of maintaining ball security with these weather conditions, but when you lead by 23 points you have earned the right to chance your arm.

By Luke Pentony

Both sides are making changes, with Piper Duck among those coming onto the field.

The Wallaroos are hoping to use Duck as an impact player, given her ability on both sides of the ball.

Anyone who saw her tackle on Canadian winger Aurora Bowie in Sacramento two weeks ago will know how devastating she can be in defence.

Duck has replaced Lily Bone in the Wallaroos' back-row.

By Luke Pentony

Wallaroos fullback Waiaria Ellis needed attention for a leg injury.

The 18-year-old is limping at the moment after a break in play, but is staying on the field.

By Luke Pentony

The second half is being played amid wet conditions.

We just saw the Black Ferns lose possession on their own line-out throw, with the ball appearing to be slippery as a bar of soap.

Key Event

By Luke Pentony

The Black Ferns add to their lead!

Forcing a turnover from the Wallaroos, the Black Ferns built presure with patient phase play as they edged their way towards the line.

Veisinia Mahutariki-Fakalelu was on hand to dot the ball down, before the conversion was kicked for a 28-5 advantage on the scoreboard.

By Luke Pentony

The second half gets going!

Can the Wallaroos claw their way back on the scoreboard?

Or will the Black Ferns shift gears and extend their lead?

By Luke Pentony

The Wallaroos showed fight in the first half but the Black Ferns know when to apply pressure on both sides of the ball.

The visitors were stung by Siokapesi Palu Sekona's try, replying with two unanswered five-pointers.

Possession has roughly been shared, and the Wallaroos should perhaps have another try on the board.

They have wasted some attacking opportunities deep inside Black Ferns' territory.

Still, there's no lack of effort from the Wallaroos against such a well-drilled unit like the Black Ferns.

Key Event

By Luke Pentony

We head for oranges, with the Black Ferns holding a 16-point advantage.

The visitors deserve their lead, although there have been some positives in attack for the Wallaroos.

But the home side will need to improve their defence in the second 40.

Key Event

By Luke Pentony

The Black Ferns have a third try, scored by Ayesha Leti-I'iga!

That's a double now for the Black Ferns winger.

The Black Ferns produced some brilliant support play to stretch the Wallaroos' defence.

Renee Holmes converted from wide out, and the visitors lead 21-5 close to half-time.

By Jamie McKinnell

Topic: National Parks

Surf lifesavers noticed the whale carcass on Saturday morning on the southern end of Era Beach. ( Supplied: SLSNSW )

A number of beaches at Sydney's Royal National Park have been closed due to increased shark activity in waters near a whale carcass.

Surf Life Saving NSW says there have been reports of large white and bull sharks in the water.

Beachgoers are warned to avoid the area, with beaches expected to stay closed for at least 24 hours.

Several popular beaches in Sydney's Royal National Park have been closed due to increased shark activity after a large whale carcass washed up on a rock platform.

Surf lifesavers noticed the whale early on Saturday morning on the southern end of Era Beach when they showed up for patrols.

Garie, Wattamolla, Era and Burning Palms have been closed as a result of the shark activity.

Shark surveillance drones and jet skis are patrolling the area. ( ABC News )

Shark surveillance drones and jet skis have been relocated to keep watch over the area.

"The lifesavers are reporting a significant amount of sharks visibly off the beach and around the rock platform," Surf Life Saving NSW (SLSNSW) CEO Stephen Pearce said.

"Our warning is, 'Don't go in the water'

"We can't prevent people from going in the water, but knowing just how many sharks are there and the reports of larger white and bull sharks in the water, they're not the fish you want to be swimming in the same water with."

Beachgoers are being advised to avoid surfing, swimming, diving or spearfishing.

Beachgoers are warned to stay out of the water. ( ABC News )

The species of the whale is unclear.

"It looks like it's been decaying for a little while out to sea," Mr Pearce said.

He said the organisation will now work with the National Parks and Wildlife Service to keep the beaches shut, likely for at least 24 hours.

"National Parks will have to make arrangements to try and come in and determine what they're going to do with the carcass.

"I think they're obviously going to have to remove it."

Mr Pearce said SLSNSW chose to issue an alert because of the long weekend, the "high visitation" area and the amount of sharks in the water.

By Michael Doyle

Topic: NRL

The Melbourne Storm have lost six matches in a row for the first time since 2002. ( AAP: Joel Carrett )

Melbourne captain Harry Grant has defended coach Craig Bellamy after the Storm sank to a historic low following a 48-6 belting at the hands of South Sydney.

The 42-point loss on Anzac Day was Melbourne's sixth defeat on the bounce, the first time that has happened under Bellamy and equalling the club's worst losing run.

Melbourne never looked in the contest in front of a packed house at AAMI Park, with thousands of fans heading for the exit early as the Rabbitohs recorded the club's first-ever win in the Victorian capital.

The Storm were down 24-0 at half-time and would have been kept scoreless had fullback Sualauvi Faalogo not produced an outrageous effort, kicking to himself off a kick-off in the 71st minutes, regathering the ball and then weaving through the Souths team who were set up in their kick-off formation.

"Most embarrassed I've ever been in my footy life, to be quite honest," Bellamy said in his post-match press conference.

"There's obviously a few things the off-field staff are doing wrong, and I'm included in that. So I ain't doing my job as well as I should be.

"But to come up with a performance like that, and a lack of effort like that on Anzac Day, is embarrassing. It's embarrassing."

Melbourne Storm captain Harry Grant (right) says the team is behind coach Craig Bellamy (left). ( NRL )

Melbourne's losing run began in round three when they surrendered a 14-point half-time lead to the Brisbane Broncos.

Since then, they also surrendered half-time leads to the North Queensland Cowboys (round four) and Canberra Raiders (round seven).

But three heavy defeats to Penrith (40 points), New Zealand (24 points) and Saturday's 42-point demolition has last year's grand finalists 16th on the NRL ladder.

After Harry Grant was asked if there was "buy in" from the playing group to turn the season around, Bellamy was asked if he believed he had the "buy in" from the playing group.

"That's a good question, I might not have," Bellamy said, before being interrupted by Grant who defended his coach.

"That's a silly question, you don't need to ask him that," Grant said.

"He's a modest guy and he is probably going to look to himself with these results.

"But at the end of the day, no one works harder than Craig."

The Storm travel to Brisbane next week to face the Dolphins who were also beaten on Anzac Day in a two-point loss to the Warriors in Auckland.

Earlier, Interim St George Illawarra coach Dean Young said his players were 'embarrassed' by their performance , as the Dragons conceded 11 tries in their 46-point loss to the Sydney Roosters.

By Michael Doyle

Here is where we end this NRL live blog on Anzac Day.

Thank-you for joining ABC Sport throughout today's coverage.

We will be back tomorrow to bring you more live digital coverage as Anzac Round concludes.

We hope you will join us then.

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

Melbourne Storm coach Craig Bellamy and captain Harry Grant have completed their press conference.

Bellamy did not mince words after the 48-6 loss to Souths.

"Most embarrassed I've ever been in my footy life, to be quite honest," he says.

"There's obviously a few things the off-field staff are doing wrong, and I'm included in that. So I ain't doing my job as well as I should be.

"But to come up with a performance like that, and a lack of effort like that on Anzac Day, is embarrassing. It's embarrassing."

By Michael Doyle

Wayne Bennett and Cam Murray are doing the coach-captain press conference.

I'll save you the time on Mr Bennett's answers, I think the longest reply I heard was seven words.

Murray was asked if the players were focused on the Melbourne hoodoo in the lead-up to the game.

For the Souths' lock, he said the team's main focus was ensuring they produced a good performance after last week's win over the Dragons.

"We didn't really speak too much about the record, to be honest," Murray says.

"We just wanted to focus on ourselves, and we wanted to chase consistency. We had a good win a couple of weeks ago against the Dogs and we didn't back it up the next week."

By Michael Doyle

Cody Walker has been part of many South Sydney defeats in Melbourne.

His first words to ABC Sport is not about the win, it is about playing on Anzac Day.

"It's a pretty special moment on a pretty special day. So many men and women fought for, and sacrificed so much for this great country"

Walker says the most pleasing thing about the win tonight was the way his team won.

"We've been close on many occasions down here, but they've always pipped us at the end or [we have] had a few floggings down here," says.

"It feels pretty special to finally get one up over them,

I think the most pleasing part was we started really well. and were able to take the game away from them.

I thought, in the second half, we probably let them back in with just errors, failure to get to our kicks and things like that.

"They're a quality side, and I thought we defended our line quite well."

By Michael Doyle

The Melbourne Storm are on a six-match losing streak for the first time since 2002.

That is the club's equal worst losing run. This has not happened since Craig Bellamy became coach.

Captain Harry Grant has spoken to Fox League after the 48-6 loss to South Sydney.

It's hard to say much when you're on the back of those performances.

"The preparation we've had over the past few weeks, it's just not transferring to the field at the moment," he says.

"South Sydney were really on with their game and we just gave them the game they wanted."

By Michael Doyle

At the 21st time of asking, South Sydney has won in Melbourne.

It was a remarkable 48-6 win.

And the win is even sweeter for Alex Johnston, scoring two tries and playing his 250th NRL match.

He has spoken to ABC Sport.

"Obviously heard the chat all week that, we haven't beaten them here," Johnston says.

"But at the end of the day, if we play the footy we know we can, we knew we were gonna get the win tonight. So we're super glad."

Johnston described tonight as a "dream milestone".

"250. It is pretty special. Hopefully I've got 50 more left in me and get that 300 [matches]."

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

— reporting by AAP

Melbourne has slumped to a historic low under coach Craig Bellamy, suffering an embarrassing 48-6 loss to a hoodoo-busting South Sydney in their Anzac Day clash.

The Rabbitohs celebrated their first win in Melbourne, taking 28 years and 21 matches to break the streak, and they did it in style.

The thumping result was the Storm's sixth-straight loss this season, which they last registered back in 2002 under Mark Murray, before Bellamy took over a year later.

It was their worst result at AAMI Park and their biggest anywhere since 2003.

With just two wins for the season, Melbourne are now in danger of missing the finals for the first time under Bellamy and their task could be even greater with superstar halfback Jahrome Hughes forced off with an apparent arm injury.

Souths were almost unstoppable in the first half, surging to a 24-0 lead with Alex Johnston bagging a double among his side's five tries.

Backing up from his own haul of four tries last round, Latrell Mitchell had a hand in both, batting on a ball to his winger for the visitors to open the scoring in the eighth minute.

Melbourne's first-half statistics were horror viewing for the large crowd, only completing 12 of 19 sets while they made zero line-breaks compared to Souths' eight.

They also made seven errors with mistakes by Sua Faalogo and Nick Meaney both handing over possession for the Rabbitohs to score.

Bellamy gave the team a huge half-time spray before striding out of the changeroom to leave the senior players and assistant coaches to find a way out of the funk.

The Storm looked like they had finally made it onto the scoreboard seven minutes into the second half, but the bunker ruled Trent Loiero had promoted the ball as he attempted to ground it over the line.

Keaon Koloamatangi and Sean Keppie also deserved credit for their desperate defence.

Tallis Duncan rubbed salt into Melbourne's wounds, spraying Cameron Munster after pushing off both the Storm five-eighth and Jack Howarth as he scored his second of three tries.

Campbell Graham also grabbed a double, the winger diving across for his team's eighth try in the 66th minute.

Faalogo broke the hosts' duck three minutes later in surprising fashion when he scooped his own short kick-off to split the defence to score a brilliant individual try.

It was Melbourne's first line-break of the night, but the visitors still had the final say with Duncan's third four-pointer.

The only blight on the Rabbitohs' night was the loss of Brandon Smith, with the burly forward re-injuring his problematic calf.

By Michael Doyle

Icing on the cake.

Souths marched into Melbourne's territory for one more raid.

Tallis Duncan charged onto the ball and powered his way to the line.

Three tries to Tallis Duncan.

Nine tries to Souths.

One sensational performance.

Storm 6

Rabbitohs 48

Key Event

By Michael Doyle

My goodness.

Has Melbourne fullback Sualauvi Faalogo scored the Try of the Year?

Faalogo does the kick-off. He is the man who does the kick-off .

He grubbers it off the tee, and there are no Souths players in front of him.

Faalogo sprints and regathers his own kick off, then weaves through the scattered Souths team who were set up to return a kick off, and he scores.

Storm 6

Rabbitohs 42

By Michael Doyle

Latrell Mitchell has just kicked a field goal from 42 metres.

It is a wonderful kick.

Mitchell turns to the crowd, extends his arms, as if to say 'are you not entertained?'

Storm 0

Rabbitohs 42

By Michael Doyle

IT'S EIGHT TRIES.

Campbell Graham has a double.

More boos at AAMI Park. More fans are heading for the exits.

This is a belting. This is a smashing.

Souths look like they were going to score in the lead-up.

Latrell Mitchell went close.

Then Tevita Tatola went close.

Both of those efforts were in the middle of the field, sucking in Melbourne defenders, and leaving the wings exposed.

Mitchell kicks the goal.

SOUTHS HAVE 40 POINTS.

Storm 0

Souths 40

By Michael Doyle

At kick-off, AAMI Park was packed to the rafters.

You can see on the TV broadcast that there are A LOT of empty seats.

Boos are echoing around the stadium.

This just never happens in Melbourne.

By Michael Doyle

Tallis Duncan has a second try.

Duncan bumps off Cam Munster, then palms off Jack Howarth to score.

Storm 0

Rabbitohs 34

By Michael Doyle

Alex Johnston makes a huge run up the middle.

It comes just two plays after Melbourne again lost the ball attacking the Souths' goal-line. And it was a poor error. Jahrome Hughes tried to jump over a defender and pass at the same time.

Johnston ran 40 metres, before being tripped up by Melbourne fullback Sualauvi Faalogo.

But the Bunnies are on the charge again.

By Michael Doyle

Souths kicked the ball to Melbourne's Manaia Waitere, who caught the ball but was then thrown into touch by three Souths defenders.

That gave the Bunnies another set at the Storm line.

Souths score again. Interchange Euan Aitken charges onto a pass from short range, and he muscles his way to the line.

Aitken just wanted it more. There were four Storm players who tried to tackle him.

Storm 0

Rabbitohs 28

By Michael Doyle

Melbourne was attacking the Souths' goal-line again.

The ball goes to Jahrome Hughes on the right, as ref Adam Gee calls for six-again.

HUGHES KICKS.

It was a poor grubber kick, collected by Latrell Mitchell.

Was that desperation?

Did Hughes know it was six-again?

Storm 0

Rabbitohs 24

By Michael Doyle

Melbourne is camped on the Souths goal-line.

With another penalty and a six-again restart, they have about 15 straight plays at the line.

There is a kick to the right wing, with Will Warbrick jumping for the ball.

The ball hits the ground, the Latrell collects the ball in his own in-goal, and he runs 60 metres downfield.

That ends the Melbourne attack.

Storm 0

Rabbitohs 24

By Michael Doyle

Souths have the ball at halfway, but there is a knock-on.

The Storm are awarded the scrum.

PENALTY.

Souths five-eighth Cody Walker has grabbed the footy and thrown it. The ball hits Joe Chan in the head.

I can't tell if he was throwing the ball in annoyance or if he was actually aiming to throw it at Stefano Utoikamanu.

Either way, poor Joe Chan got whacked in the noggin.

Storm 0

Rabbitohs 24

By Michael Doyle

Melbourne is celebrating a try.

Lock Trent Loiero crashes over, and he is awarded the try.

HANG ON. The Bunker wants to look at this.

There is a double-movement.

Loiero grounded the ball just inches from the line, and then he promoted the ball-carrying arm.

That is a good spot from the Bunker.

Storm 0

Rabbitohs 24

By Michael Doyle

Melbourne just had its best three plays.

Stefano Utoikamanu takes a strong run, makes 15 metres, and gets a quick play-the-ball.

Harry Grant darts from dummy-half, and then a pass outside, then inside to Sualauvi Faalogo, which leads to a line break.

Harry Grant darts again, kicks, and Souths fumbles that kick.

The Storm have a scrum, 30 metres from the Souths line.

Storm 0

Rabbitohs 24
